119759.note: The AJW community directory (posted March 2013, last changed Dec 2015, archived April 2016): 'For more than 20 years, Oneg Shabbos V'Yom Tov has brought relief to needy families in the Twin Cities' (food packages, help for Russian immigrants, scholarships, needy brides and grooms), at 400 Marie Ave. W. (Lubavitch House), so it began before 1995. Today's directory still has the same words. A department of Upper Midwest Merkos (117647) on chabad.org; its listing is in the first online directory (2004).

684361.name: It's Good To Know
684361.note: Rabbi Manis Friedman's nonprofit (itsgoodtoknow.org); its own site gives no year. IRS: 'Its Good To Know Inc' (Brooklyn, NY), exempt since April 2005 (ProPublica's IRS data), so it existed by then. Its chabad.org listing went up June 4 2008.

1096297.name: Chabad U of M - The Rohr Center for Jewish Student Life
1096297.note: TC Jewfolk (5 Sept 2025): Rabbi Yitzi and Chavi Steiner 'started Chabad at the University of Minnesota, which celebrates its 15th anniversary of being on campus this year'; the U of M had no Chabad, though the rest of the Big Ten 'at that time – 2010' had one. Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 17 2010. Now 1121 University Avenue SE.

1560476.name: Chabad of Greater St. Paul
1560476.note: Its own About page (posted 4 Dec 2011, read through Firecrawl): 'Rabbi Zalman & Nechama founded Chabad of Greater S. Paul in the fall of 2011.' Its chabad.org listing went up July 1 2011. The AJW directory gives 998 Stratford Road, Mendota Heights.

2027612.name: Chabad Jewish Center of North Dakota
2027612.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 28 May 2025): 'When she and her husband, Rabbi Yonah Grossman, moved to Fargo in 2011'; Valley News Live (5 Dec 2021): 'Rabbi Yonah and his wife Esti Grossman moved to Fargo in 2011 to open the Chabad Jewish Center'. Medium: Lubavitch.com (on CrownHeights.info, 21 Nov 2012) calls them the Grossmans 'who have recently moved to Fargo', announced at that month's Kinus, and the chabad.org listing went up Nov 6 2012. Now 1234 Broadway N.

3368473.name: Chabad Young Professionals Uptown Minneapolis
3368473.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 12 Jan 2017): Rabbi Sholom and Mushky Brook, 'co-directors of the Uptown Chabad of Minneapolis and its Chabad Young Professionals group', were asked by Rabbi Mordechai Grossbaum to start it; 'The couple received the go-ahead in March; a few months later, they made the move' (March 2016, so mid-2016). Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 18 2016.

3451535.name: Chabad Jewish Center of South Dakota
3451535.note: JTA (in the St. Louis Jewish Light, 27 Dec 2016): 'Rabbi Mendel and Mussie Alperowitz and their children arrived on Dec. 24 in Sioux Falls, where they will open a Chabad center.' Its chabad.org listing went up Nov 16 2016. Now 4901 S Isabel Pl, Suite 200.

5228285.name: Chabad of Macalester-Groveland
5228285.note: No start date found. COLlive (29 Dec 2022): 'Chabad of Macalester-Groveland is Minnesota's newest Chabad House', Rabbi Tzemach and Mushky Feller, for St. Paul's campuses; before it, students came to Lubavitch House in West St. Paul. AJW directory: 1546 Portland Ave. Its chabad.org listing went up Sept 14 2021, so it existed by then.

5316650.name: Chabad of Maple Grove
5316650.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 4 April 2022): 'Rabbi Nissi Naparstek moved to Maple Grove, Minnesota, last November' (Nov 2021); 'The Naparsteks have only been in Minnesota for four months'. Its chabad.org listing went up Nov 18 2021.

6150594.name: The Gan Rochester Preschool
6150594.note: Rochester Post Bulletin (2 Sept 2022): 'Greene opened the doors of the lower level of her southwest Rochester home in October 2020 as a family child care center called The Gan.' Chana Greene directs it, as part of Chabad of Southern Minnesota (117646). Its chabad.org listing went up Nov 1 2023.

7417922.name: Chabad of Eden Prairie
7417922.note: TC Jewfolk (31 Aug 2026): 'A new Chabad is launching in Eden Prairie'; Rabbi Schneur and Sheina Matusof will lead it; 'The idea came to the couple in April'; Rosh Hashanah 2026 programs planned. Its chabad.org listing went up July 22 2026.

117539.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Arizona
117539.note: Jewish News of Greater Phoenix (8 June 2026, 'Chabad celebrates 50 years in Arizona'): 'Shortly after arriving in January 1977, Zalman and Tzipi mailed over 5,000 shalach manos'; 'Chabad also organized a megillah reading in February 1977'. The Jewish News (8 Feb 2002, its 25th anniversary): 'The synagogue first met in a garage at Third Avenue and McDowell Road. In 1978, Chabad moved to Maryland Avenue and 15th Street'; 'In 1990, the congregation moved to its current location at 2110 E. Lincoln Drive in Phoenix' (bought in 1989, per the 2026 article). One Jewish News piece (2 June 2026) has them moving to Phoenix 'in 1976'.

earlier.where: a garage at Third Avenue and McDowell Road, Phoenix
Maryland Avenue and 15th Street, Phoenix

117540.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Tucson
117540.note: Jewish News of Greater Phoenix (8 Feb 2002): 'In 1984, Rabbi Yossi and Chana Shemtov started Chabad of Tucson.' Arizona Jewish Post (1 May 2025): 'Shemtov has led the congregation since 1984.' The Arizona Jewish Post of 16 Feb 2017 dates their sending to 1983: 'The expansion of Chabad to other cities in Arizona began in 1983, when Rabbi Yossie and Chanie Shemtov were sent by the Rebbe to establish Chabad Tucson and Chabad activities at the University of Arizona.' Kept as 1984, when they began there. At 2443 East 4th Street (Young Israel-Chabad Tucson) today.

117912.name: Chabad of Scottsdale
117912.note: lubavitch.com (4 Oct 2021, 'Scottsdale's Jewish Community Turns Thirty'): 'When Rabbi Yossi and Dina Levertov moved to Scottsdale in 1992'. The Jewish News (8 Feb 2002): 'In 1992, Levertov's brother, Rabbi Yossi Levertov, started Chabad of Scottsdale with his wife Dina.' The Jewish News 'Synagogue timeline' (17 Aug 2007): '1992 Chabad of Scottsdale'. COLlive (10 Feb 2017): 'the 25th anniversary of Chabad of Scottsdale'. Now The Weksler Chabad Center, 10215 North Scottsdale Road.

119846.name: Mazal Tov Gifts - Book Store
119846.note: No year of its own: Chabad of Scottsdale's gift shop, a department of Chabad of Scottsdale (117912, 1992) on chabad.org. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then.

3012050.name: Kosher Restaurant (Kitchen 18)
3012050.note: The listing's site is Thekitchen18.com, a department of Chabad of Scottsdale on chabad.org. The Jewish News (31 Jan 2013): 'The restaurant that was part of Scottsdale Café Market and Deli has transformed into Kitchen 18, a kosher restaurant'; '(Kitchen 18 is supervised by Chabad.)' Medium: new in Jan 2013, so it may have opened late in 2012. Its chabad.org listing went up July 21 2015.

118252.name: Chabad of the East Valley
118252.note: The Jewish News (21 Nov 1997, 'Chabad programs under way in Chandler'): 'Chabad of the Southeast Valley started out this year with more than 100 people attending its High Holiday services at the Chandler Windmill Inn'; the money 'went to hire 24-year-old Rabbi Mendy Deitsch of Crown Heights, N.Y., to head the organization'. The Jewish News 'Synagogue timeline' (2007): '1997 Chabad of the East Valley'. Now 875 North McClintock Drive.

118414.name: Chabad of the West Valley
118414.note: The Jewish News (1 Sept 2000, 'Chabad opens in Glendale'): 'Chabad of the West Valley, under the leadership of Rabbi Sholom Lew, will open its doors in late September for Rosh Hashana'; 'Located on the grounds of Benley Manor, a kosher retirement community opening soon in Glendale'. The 2007 'Synagogue timeline': '2000 Chabad of the West Valley'. Now 6635 W Happy Valley Road.

earlier.where: the grounds of Benley Manor, a kosher retirement community, Glendale

118615.name: Chabad at Arizona State University
118615.note: The Jewish News (19 Sept 2003, 'Chabad presence at ASU'): 'Rabbi Shmuel Tiechtel, along with his wife, Chana, and infant son, Tzvi, will arrive in Tempe from Brooklyn, N.Y., after the High Holidays.' The 2007 'Synagogue timeline': '2003 Chabad at ASU'. At 971 S. Ash Ave. (the Rohr Chabad House) by 2007, as today.

150719.name: Chabad Lubavitch of North Phoenix
150719.note: The Jewish News (9 April 2004, 'Chabad to expand to North Valley'): 'Rabbi Mendy Levertov, son of Rabbi Zalman and Tzipi Levertov, who founded Chabad of Arizona 27 years ago, will begin programming for Chabad of North Phoenix after Passover.' 'Initially, he and his wife Leah will offer classes in private homes.' The 2007 'Synagogue timeline': '2004 Chabad of North Phoenix'. Now 22044 North 44th Street.

350478.name: Chabad of Anthem
350478.note: The Jewish News (26 Aug 2005, 'Chabad comes to Anthem'): 'Chabad of Arizona plans to open a center in Anthem and to offer Talmud Torah in the young community north of Phoenix beginning Sept. 18.' Before that: 'In May 2004, Levertov met with 35 Jewish residents of Anthem, which led to his son-in-law Rabbi Yossi Friedman leading High Holiday services at the Hampton Inn there last October.' The 2007 'Synagogue timeline': '2005 Chabad of Anthem'.

625537.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Mesa
625537.note: The Arizona Republic (22 Sept 2006, reposted on 'Lubavitch In the News'): 'Chabad of Arizona will hold Rosh Hashana services at the Mesa Convention Center'; '"We're looking at the prospects of opening a Chabad center in Mesa," Blotner said.' By Dec 2006 the Jewish News listed a 'Chabad of Mesa' public menorah lighting, and its 2007 'Synagogue timeline' has '2006 Chabad of Mesa'. Rabbi Laibel (Laib) Blotner leads it; now 941 S Maple. Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 14 2008.

359494.name: Chabad of Flagstaff
359494.note: The Jewish News (17 Feb 2006, 'Chabad opens new center in Flagstaff'): 'Chabad of Arizona is opening a new center in Flagstaff next week. Rabbi Dovie Shapiro and his wife, Chaya, will move from Brooklyn, N.Y., to open Chabad of Flagstaff at 22 E. Elm Ave. in downtown Flagstaff'. Now 930 W University Avenue.

earlier.where: 22 E. Elm Ave., downtown Flagstaff

157392.name: Arizona Jewish Russian Programs
157392.note: The Jewish News (13 Dec 1996, 'One little candle'): 'Now, Chabad's Rabbi Don Hayman has taken over much of the interchange' with the Valley's Russian immigrants; its calendar of 6 Dec 1996 lists a 'Russian-speaking Hanukkah party' at Chabad of Phoenix, and on 26 Sept 1997 'Rabbi Don Hayman, Russian outreach and program director at the Phoenix Chabad center'. The Jewish News (12 Jan 2001, 'Free to be Jewish'): 'In the four years since the programs' inception, they have served more than 2,000 new Americans.' Both put the start in 1996. Its chabad.org listing went up July 29 2004.

976025.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Fountain Hills
976025.note: lubavitch.com (3 Oct 2018): 'Since their arrival in 2010 until this month, the Lipskiers have led services and communal events from their home and office on a quiet residential street.' The Jewish News (on COLlive, 2 Oct 2018): 'Lipskier founded Chabad of Fountain Hills in 2010'. Its new home, the Chabad Edelman Jewish Center at 16830 E. Avenue of the Fountains (the former Gridley's store), opened for Rosh Hashana 2018. Its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Aug 31 2009.

earlier.where: the Lipskiers' home and office, Fountain Hills

992582.name: Chabad of Downtown
992582.note: The Jewish News (2 Feb 2021): 'Levertov's son, Rabbi Levi Levertov, started the work of building a Chabad presence downtown 11 years ago, while also launching and directing Smile on Seniors Arizona.' Its first full-time couple, Rabbi Dovber and Chana Dechter, the directors now, 'moved to Phoenix this December' (Dec 2020; lubavitch.com, 24 Aug 2021). Medium: a count back, and its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Sept 29 2009. Now 1515 West Palm Lane.

1090387.name: Smile on Seniors
1090387.note: The Jewish News ('Valley View', 18 Dec 2009): Chabad 'launched a volunteer program to serve senior citizens in the Metro Phoenix area on a daily basis'; 'The national program will be coordinated and run locally by Rabbi Levi Levertov and his wife, Chani.' Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 14 2010.

4540280.name: Jewish Care Network
4540280.note: The Jewish News (26 Oct 2021): Rabbi Moshe and Sashie Levertov: 'Last year, the couple launched the Jewish Care Network to ensure that people don't face an illness alone.' Medium: its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Nov 4 2019. At 2110 E Lincoln Drive (Chabad of Arizona).

5276310.name: Cteen Phoenix
5276310.note: The Jewish News ('Valley View', 5 Aug 2011, 'Chabad hires rabbi for new teen program'): 'Chabad of Arizona has hired Rabbi Dov Levertov to run C-Teen, a program for Jewish teens throughout the Valley'; 'The kickoff event will be at 4 p.m. Sunday, Aug. 21'. The same program after: CTEEN at Chabad of Phoenix, 2110 E. Lincoln Drive (Jewish News, Oct 2013); with Rabbi Tzvi Rimler by Dec 2017 (Jewish News, Feb 2018); this listing (the Rimlers, 2110 E Lincoln Drive) went up Oct 12 2021; 'Rabbi Tzvi Rimler, director of CTeen Phoenix' (Jewish News, 12 March 2026).

1184673.name: Camp Gan Izzy
1184673.note: No year of its own: Chabad Tucson's day camp (a department of 117540), run by Feigie Ceitlin, youth director of Chabad of Tucson. The Arizona Jewish Post (15 June 2012): 'Chabad's Camp Gan Izzy, for ages 2-12, runs June 25-July 20', with 'three of last year's out-of-town counselors' returning. Its chabad.org listing went up April 20 2010, so it existed by then.

455508.name: Chabad on River
455508.note: No start date found. Rabbi Rami and Chani Bigelman's center: the Jewish News (8 Feb 2002): 'Rabbi Rami and Chana Bigelman joined them in 2000' (Chabad of Tucson); the Arizona Jewish Post (24 March 2011): 'Chabad on River will welcome its first Sefer Torah on Sunday, April 10'. Its chabad.org listing went up Dec 12 2006, so it existed by then. Now 3916 E Fort Lowell Road.

5607924.name: Chabad House at the University of Arizona
5607924.note: Arizona Jewish Post (on CrownHeights.info, 22 June 2006): Rabbi Yossie Winner, 25, 'moved to Tucson last July from Brooklyn with his wife, Naomi, 23, to establish a Chabad House on the University of Arizona campus.' Chabad was 'active on the UA campus in the early 1980s' through Chabad Tucson (Arizona Jewish Post, 14 July 2015). The Winners hosted students in their two-bedroom house and a backyard tent until the Rohr Chabad Jewish Student Center at 1436 E. Drachman, this listing's address, was built (expected to open Dec 2015). This listing went up on Oct 25 2022 and names Rabbi Shmulie and Sarah Shanowitz; the Arizona Daily Star (17 May 2026): 'Rabbi Shmulie Shanowitz, director of the Chabad House on campus'.

earlier.where: the Winners' two-bedroom house and a backyard tent, near Euclid Avenue and Speedway Boulevard, Tucson

1279033.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Goodyear
1279033.note: CrownHeights.info (27 April 2021): 'In 2010 Rabbi Berel and Chana Zaklikofsky made a lifetime commitment to the Jewish community of Goodyear, AZ, founding the Chabad Jewish Center.' The Jewish News ('Valley View', 17 June 2011, 'Chabad opens center in Goodyear'): they 'moved to Arizona from Brooklyn, N.Y., last week to start Chabad Jewish Center of Goodyear'; before that he 'visited Arizona last December to host a menorah-lighting celebration at Goodyear Community Park'. Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 19 2010. Medium: founded 2010 (the listing, the Dec 2010 lighting), opened with the move in June 2011. Now 14295 W La Reata Avenue.

1681679.name: Chabad of Gilbert Jewish Center
1681679.note: East Valley Tribune (on CrownHeights.info, 6 Sept 2012): Rabbi Shimi Ash and his wife, Chavie, with their son 'moved about two months ago from New York' to establish the Chabad Jewish Center, in time for the High Holidays. Its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Nov 17 2011. Now 4475 E. Carriage Way.

1689667.name: Chabad of Oro Valley
1689667.note: Arizona Jewish Post (17 May 2012): 'Chabad of Tucson has appointed Rabbi Ephraim Zimmerman to be the first full-time rabbi serving the spiritual, religious and educational needs of Oro Valley Jews.' Arizona Jewish Post (16 Feb 2017): 'In 2012, Rabbi Ephraim Zimmerman and his wife, Mushkie, were brought to Arizona to found Chabad of Oro Valley'. Its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Nov 25 2011.

2364351.name: Chabad of Paradise Valley
2364351.note: The Jewish News (19 Feb 2014): 'Chabad of Arizona has announced the opening of a new center: Chabad of Paradise Valley. The center will be run by Rabbi Shlomy and Chaya Levertov.' Its first programs, among them 'a Shabbat dinner scheduled for March 14', were to be held in a private home. Its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Oct 29 2013.

2666160.name: Chabad of Prescott
2666160.note: The Jewish News (10 Dec 2014): 'Rabbi Elie and Bracha Filler recently relocated to Prescott to open Chabad of Prescott and plan to hold its first event during Hanukkah.' Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 21 2014. Now 418 N Washington Ave.

3181882.name: Chabad of Cochise County
3181882.note: lubavitch.com (22 Aug 2016, 'Chabad Opens in Cochise County, Arizona'): the Jews of the county 'convinced Rabbi Bentzion and Chaya Shemtov to move down there with their two children, and open a Chabad House'; 'the twenty-first branch of Chabad Lubavitch to open in the state of Arizona, and the first in Cochise County'. COLlive (2 Jan 2026): 'We arrived in Sierra Vista just before Rosh Hashanah of 2016'. Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 26 2016.

3590177.name: Chabad of Sedona
3590177.note: Rabbi Mendel and Fraydee Kessler. Its chabad.org listing went up March 13 2017, and the IRS lists 'Chabad Of Sedona Inc' as exempt from May 2017 (ProPublica). COLlive (31 Aug 2018): Kessler, 'who was a chaplain at Ironwood and is now the director of Chabad of Sedona, Arizona'. No report of its opening found; its own site gives no year. Medium: from these records, not a statement. Now 140 Coffee Pot Drive.

4927362.name: Chabad of Casa Grande
4927362.note: COLlive (25 Jan 2021): 'Rabbi Moshe and Chaya Sasonkin (nee Bigelman) were appointed as the first Shluchim to Casa Grande'; 'the Sasonkis say they are looking forward to moving down there'. Casa Grande Dispatch (7 May 2021): 'Rabbi Moshe Sasonkin and his wife Chaya recently moved to Casa Grande and are hoping to connect with the area Jewish community.' So they moved in early 2021; ChabadInfo (25 Jan 2021): 'After visiting Casa Grande, AZ in 2020 Rabbi Moshe & Chaya Sasonkin decided to relocate and establish a Chabad Center'. Its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Nov 10 2020.

5157809.name: Chabad of Vail, Arizona
5157809.note: The Vail Voice (4 Aug 2021, 'Vail Gets First Rabbi'): 'In time for the upcoming High Holidays, Rabbi Sruly and Chavie Shemtov from Brooklyn, NY, are set to establish a new Chabad Jewish Center'. COLlive (21 July 2021): they 'have established Chabad Jewish Center in Vail'. Its chabad.org listing went up June 17 2021.

5370570.name: Chabad on 7th Street
5370570.note: No start date found: Rabbi Buzzy and Chaya Ajzenszmidt's 'Chabad 7th - Serving the 7th Street community' (its site, read through Firecrawl, gives no year; no news found). Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 18 2022, so it existed by then.

5529178.name: Chabad Israeli Center
5529178.note: COLlive (15 Dec 2022): 'Rabbi Shneur and Chanie Feigin have established the Chabad Israel Center in Phoenix, which will be serving the Hebrew-speaking population'; 'They arrive with their 3 children.' Its chabad.org listing went up June 16 2022. Now 4523 E Hearn Road.

5566144.name: Chabad of Lake Havasu City
5566144.note: CrownHeights.info (13 Nov 2022): Rabbi Mendel and Itta Super 'are moving in just three weeks to build the only Chabad House in Arizona's largest and most isolated county'. Its chabad.org listing went up July 6 2022. Now 116 Acoma Blvd N.

5590394.name: Chabad of Downtown - South Scottsdale
5590394.note: The Jewish News (4 March 2025): 'The Bronsteins took the helm of the Chabad Young Professionals of Scottsdale group in 2022', and later 'moved to open Chabad of Old Town-South Scottsdale'. Its chabad.org listing (Rabbi Shmuli and Mushkie Bronstein, young professionals) went up Oct 24 2022. Medium: when the Old Town center itself opened isn't stated.

5597418.name: Chabad of Ahwatukee
5597418.note: The Jewish News (25 Jan 2023): Rabbi Levi and Chaya Minsky: 'A couple of months ago, not long before Chanukah, their shared dream became a reality'; they 'arrived in Ahwatukee, a small city in the East Valley'. Its chabad.org listing went up Oct 25 2022.

5818525.name: Chabad Bukharian Center
5818525.note: The Jewish News (3 Oct 2023, 'Phoenix Bukharian synagogue reopens under new leadership'): 'The CBC is the new iteration of what had been the Bukharian Jewish Congress of Arizona, which closed its doors in 2021'; 'Rabbi Emanuel Shimonov is the center's new spiritual leader.' Its chabad.org listing went up March 16 2023. At 17421 N 6th Place.

5954255.name: Chabad of Moon Valley & GCU
5954255.note: CrownHeights.info (9 Aug 2023): 'Rabbi Shneur and Esther Wolfman have been announced as the newest Shluchim heading to the city'. The Jewish News (21 Dec 2023): 'On Dec. 10, Chabad of Moon Valley celebrated its first big community holiday event at Moon Valley Park in Phoenix', by 'The recently arrived shluchim'. Its chabad.org listing went up May 23 2023.

6422398.name: Chabad of Surprise
6422398.note: CrownHeights.info (6 July 2024): Rabbi Shlomy and Batya (nee Lew) Ceitlin 'will be heading to Surprise, Arizona to start a new Chabad Center for the growing Jewish population'. lubavitch.com (24 Sept 2024): 'when the Ceitlins moved to town to create a center'. Its chabad.org listing went up July 2 2024.

6448214.name: Chabad of NE Rural Arizona
6448214.note: The Jewish News (8 July 2024): Rabbi Yaakov and Tiferes Cahnman 'are heading up Chabad of Rural Arizona, a new Chabad program'; 'the first Chabad of Rural Arizona event in Pinetop-Lakeside last month' (June 2024). Its chabad.org listing went up July 17 2024 (1000 N Beeline Hwy, Payson).

6471783.name: Chabad of San Tan Valley
6471783.note: CrownHeights.info, 4 Dec 2024 ('Chabad Responds to Tragedy by Expanding Global Outreach: 100 New Centers To Be Established'): Keren Hashluchim seed funding 'for one hundred new Chabad centers in underserved areas'; among 'The Fifty New Shluchim': 'Rabbi Mendel and Rivky Wolowik at Chabad of San Tan Valley, AZ' (a new community Chabad House). Its chabad.org listing went up 17 July 2024; its own site gives no year.

6659224.name: Chabad of Buckeye
6659224.note: lubavitch.com (22 July 2025): 'This summer, Rabbi Mendy and Shterna Goldstein launched Chabad of Buckeye to serve the city's estimated 1,000 Jews'. Its chabad.org listing went up earlier, on Nov 18 2024.

7343104.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Maricopa City
7343104.note: The Jewish News (2 June 2026): Chabad of Arizona is 'marking its half-century anniversary with the opening of a brand-new Carefree center, as well as a center in Maricopa.' Rabbi Dov Ber and Rivka Fridman; its chabad.org listing went up May 26 2026.

7369479.name: Chabad of Carefree
7369479.note: The Jewish News (2 June 2026): 'Chabad of Arizona recently announced that it is expanding to incorporate a new Chabad center, bringing Jewish learning and connection to the North Valley communities of Carefree and Cave Creek.' Rabbi Mendel and Mussie Heller; its chabad.org listing went up June 15 2026.

117740.name: Lubavitch of Wisconsin
117740.note: Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (7 July 2019): 'Shmotkin brought the Chabad movement to Wisconsin back in October of 1968.' JTA Daily Bulletin (25 Nov 1968, 'Lubavitcher Movement Opens Wisconsin Regional Office'): 'The Lubavitcher movement has announced the opening of a new regional office in Milwaukee, Wis., Its seventh in the United States', headed by Rabbi Israel Shmotkin. Lubavitch News Service (30 Aug 1973, reprinted on lubavitch.com 7 Aug 2009): the new headquarters 'is a spacious 3 story, 33 room mansion, located at 3109 North Lake Drive, in Milwaukee', where it still is; where the office was in 1968-73 is not stated.

117738.name: Chabad Madison
117738.note: Lubavitch.com (28 July 2015, 'In The Footsteps of Their Parents'), Faygie and Yona Matusof: 'When we arrived in 1980, we were told that it's only a matter of time before we leave.' Lubavitch.com (2025, 'Chabad of Madison Unveils New Center'): 'Founded in 1980 by Rabbi Yona and Faygie Matusof, Chabad of Madison started out serving Jewish students in the University of Wisconsin.' Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle (undated, filed 31 March 2008, 'mark 25 years'): 'They married in August 1980, seven weeks before they moved to Madison.' Medium, not high: there was Chabad in Madison before them. The Daily Cardinal (24 Feb 2006): 'The international organization first appeared at UW-Madison in 1972'; the Chronicle (7 July 2019): 'In 1970, Lubavitch of Wisconsin was operating out of fewer than a half-dozen outposts, including Chabad of the East Side and Madison Chabad House.' Who ran it then is not found. 117707.name: Congregation Tzemach Tzedek
117707.note: Cleveland Jewish News (13 July 2011, Rabbi Zalman Kazen's obituary): 'The couple came to Cleveland in 1953 at the request of Lubavicher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson. While applying for a High Holiday position at what would become Zemach Zedek, he realized he was related to the Madorsky family, who founded the congregation (then known commonly as Nusach Ari Shul). Shortly after Zemach Zedek moved to Cleveland Heights in 1957, Rabbi Kazen bought his home on Glenmont Road, which served as Cleveland's original Chabad house. When Zemach Zedek's rabbi moved to Wickliffe, Rabbi Kazen was chosen to lead the congregation.' The CJN (3 July 2014): the Kazens 'brought the Chabad-Lubavitch movement to Cleveland in 1953'; Rabbi Kazen 'served as spiritual leader for more than 50 years'; Rabbi Mordechai Mendelson 'took over as Congregation Zemach Zedek's spiritual leader after the passing of Rabbi Kazen in 2011'. Quebec enterprise register (Registraire des entreprises, open data 'Registre des entreprises', file of Nov 1 2026): 'Soins Chabad' / 'Chabad Care' (NEQ 1177082709), a non-profit constituted Nov 8 2021 (Part III, Companies Act), domicile 5181 de Maisonneuve Blvd W (the listing's address). A state filing of its own corporation, entered as the year with medium confidence (owner, Nov 10: 'Filing date is either low or medium confidence, but it's data and data is data'). Its chabad.org listing went up 2022-06-30, so it existed by then. Director: Shimon Partouche.

5688626.name: Yagdil Torah
5688626.note: No founding year found yet (Nov 9: first pass only: CrownHeights.info and lubavitch.com searched by name and director, and a web search for the older centres; not dug into yet). Its chabad.org listing went up 2022-11-02, so it existed by then. Director: Shmuel Shuchat. Quebec enterprise register (Registraire des entreprises, open data 'Registre des entreprises', file of Nov 1 2026): the corporation at Suite 301, 5110 de Courtrai (the listing's address), NEQ 1163598916, was constituted Mar 22 2006 as 'CHINUCH ÉDUCATION QUALITÉ' / 'CHINUCH QUALITY EDUCATION' (to support students' education) and declared 'Congrégation Yagdil Torah' only on July 9 2025, after the listing (Nov 2 2022); whether Yagdil Torah goes back to 2006 is not shown, so not taken.

6673125.name: Chabad of Trois-Rivières
6673125.note: Chabad.org on CrownHeights.info, 29 Nov 2024: 'Rabbi Aaron and Amanda Spiro, natives of Montreal, have officially established Chabad-Lubavitch of Trois-Rivières'. Lubavitch.com, 24 Dec 2024: from 2021 they had been visiting the city once a month for Shabbat and holiday programmes. Its chabad.org listing went up 9 Dec 2024.

6729898.name: ChabadHeart
6729898.note: No founding report found (Nov 9 first pass: CrownHeights.info and lubavitch.com searched by name and director, and a web search). Quebec enterprise register (Registraire des entreprises, open data 'Registre des entreprises', file of Nov 1 2026): 'Chabad du Coeur' / 'Chabad Heart' (NEQ 3380329188), an association formed Nov 5 2024 and registered Nov 6 2024, domicile 6232 Légaré (the listing's address). A state registration of its own, entered as the year with medium confidence (owner, Nov 10: 'Filing date is either low or medium confidence, but it's data and data is data'). Its chabad.org listing went up 2025-07-02, so it existed by then. Director: Barak Hetsroni.

7251670.name: Chabad of Lachine
7251670.note: COLlive, 8 Nov 2026 ('New Shluchim to Lachine, Montreal'): 'Rabbi Fully and Goldi Wilmowsky, together with their baby Fayga, have moved to Lachine, Montreal, Quebec to establish a new Chabad Center'; 'Since arriving ... We welcomed community members for Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur services, hosted Sukkos celebrations, and established weekly Shabbos services'; 'The last synagogue in Lachine closed its doors in 1944.' Its chabad.org listing went up 13 Apr 2026.

extra-us-marlboro-cjl-kanelsky.name: Center for Jewish Life
extra-us-marlboro-cjl-kanelsky.note: Rabbi Yossi Kanelsky's center (official, directly under Merkos: owner, Nov 10, 2026). NJ Jewish News, 8 June 2011: the Central Committee of Chabad-Lubavitch Rabbis settled a challenge by Rabbi Boruch Chazanow and Rabbi Moshe Herson to his new Marlboro center (as summarized in data/extra-centers.json). Medium: one source, calling it new in mid-2011; its start is not stated. Not on chabad.org.

extra-us-fair-lawn-bris-avrohom.name: Bris Avrohom of Fair Lawn
extra-us-fair-lawn-bris-avrohom.note: Jewish Link, 6 Aug 2026 (after Rabbi Berel Zaltzman's passing; as summarized in data/extra-centers.json): founded in 1993 by Rabbi Berel and Rebbetzin Chaya Esther Zaltzman, now led by their son Rabbi Mendel and Elke Zaltzman. Medium: one secondary source. Official since the owner's word (Nov 10, 2026).

extra-us-jersey-city-bris-avrohom.name: Bris Avrohom of Jersey City
extra-us-jersey-city-bris-avrohom.note: Bris Avrohom began in Jersey City in 1979 (Rabbi Mordechai Kanelsky; Jewish Link, 28 Aug 2019, 'Bris Avrohom Celebrates Forty Years': in the early 1980s the new Soviet immigrants lived in Newark, Jersey City and Irvington; 'The third headquarters of Bris Avrohom is on 35 Cottage Street in Jersey City and is directed by Rabbi Boruch and Kreina Lepkevker'). Medium: the year is the network's start in the city; when this branch itself opened is not stated. Official since the owner's word (Nov 10, 2026).
